questions.q: A MERGE fails because two source rows match one target row. What is the fix?

options.t: Switch the target to an external table
options.why: Table type doesn't change the rule.

options.t: Add `WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN DELETE` so the extra row is removed
options.why: That acts on target rows the source lacks.

options.t: Run the MERGE twice, once per duplicate
options.why: Each run would still have both rows.

options.t: Deduplicate the source so each key appears once

questions.explain: Only one source row may match a given target row; several matches fail the merge, so deduplicate the source first.

questions.q: A replayed batch must not add rows the table already has. Which MERGE does that?

options.t: `WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT *` on a unique key, with no matched clause
`WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET *` with no insert clause at all, so existing rows are refreshed
options.why: That never adds the new rows.

options.t: `WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN DELETE`, run after the append
`WHEN MATCHED THEN DELETE` followed by an INSERT INTO

questions.explain: An insert-only MERGE on a unique key appends only records not already present: the documented way to avoid duplicates when a batch is replayed.

questions.q: A MERGE has `WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN DELETE` with no condition over a 5 TB target. What does the merge page advise?

options.t: Nothing; the clause only reads source rows
options.why: It acts on target rows and can't read source columns.

options.t: Add a condition, to avoid rewriting the whole target
Replace it with a separate TRUNCATE of the target before every MERGE
Move it before the WHEN MATCHED clause

questions.explain: WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE updates or deletes target rows the source lacks; it can't read source columns, and Databricks recommends a condition so the whole target isn't rewritten.

questions.q: A MERGE uses `UPDATE SET *` and `INSERT *`, and the source has a new column. Without schema evolution, what happens to it?

options.t: The column is added to the target
It is written to a rescued data column

questions.explain: With INSERT * / UPDATE SET *, the source must have every target column, and extra source columns are ignored unless schema evolution is on (MERGE WITH SCHEMA EVOLUTION).

questions.q: Which `_change_type` values does change data feed record for an UPDATE?

options.why: There is no merge change type.

options.t: `update` only, carrying the row's new values

questions.explain: Change records carry `_change_type` (insert, update_preimage, update_postimage, delete), `_commit_version` and `_commit_timestamp`.

questions.q: Legacy change data feed was turned on at version 40. A job asks for changes from version 10. Why can't it get them?

options.t: CDF only records changes after it was enabled
CDF keeps changes for only 10 versions, whatever the table's retention
Version numbers restart when CDF is enabled
Batch reads of CDF need a streaming query

questions.explain: CDF records changes only after it is enabled; it is not a permanent record, and its files follow the table's retention.

questions.q: How does Databricks recommend processing a table's change feed incrementally?

options.t: A scheduled `table_changes` query with versions tracked by hand
options.why: Possible, but streaming tracks versions for you.

options.t: DESCRIBE HISTORY parsed in a notebook

questions.explain: Read in batch with table_changes, or incrementally with readStream.option('readChangeFeed', 'true'); Databricks recommends Structured Streaming, which tracks versions.

questions.q: An INSERT writes an INT value into a BIGINT column of a Delta table. What happens?

options.t: It fails: types must match exactly
options.why: A safe cast is tried first.

options.t: It succeeds by a safe cast
The value is stored as NULL

questions.explain: Schema enforcement first tries a safe cast; an INT into a BIGINT column succeeds. An unknown column fails with UNRESOLVED_COLUMN.WITH_SUGGESTION.

questions.q: A column must be renamed without rewriting data files. What does the table need?
questions.explain: Rename and drop without rewriting need column mapping; a dropped column's data stays in the files until REORG TABLE and VACUUM.

questions.q: Which is the recommended way to let one write add new columns?

options.t: Per-write evolution, such as `.option('mergeSchema', 'true')` or `MERGE WITH SCHEMA EVOLUTION`
`ALTER TABLE ... REPLACE COLUMNS` before every write
`overwriteSchema` on an append, which adds the new columns without rewriting data
options.why: overwriteSchema is for overwrites that change the schema.

questions.explain: The session setting is legacy; Databricks recommends per-write evolution, which takes precedence. New columns are added at the end.

questions.q: Two DataFrames have the same columns in different orders. Which union matches columns by name?

options.why: UNION removes duplicates, matching by position.

questions.explain: union() and unionAll() keep duplicates and match by position; unionByName() matches by name, and allowMissingColumns=True fills missing columns with null.

questions.q: DataFrame `union()` behaves like which SQL operator?

options.t: EXCEPT: rows of the second are removed

questions.explain: DataFrame union() keeps duplicates, like SQL UNION ALL; add .distinct() to deduplicate.

questions.q: Rows from `orders` must be kept only when no matching customer exists. Which join type?

options.why: Semi keeps rows that do match.
A left join keeps all rows, with nulls for no match.

questions.explain: how may be inner, cross, outer/full, left, right, semi/left_semi or anti/left_anti; anti keeps the rows with no match.

questions.q: A stream uses `dropDuplicates(['event_id'])`. What bounds the state it keeps?

options.t: The trigger interval of the query

options.why: Dropping duplicates on a stream keeps state.

questions.explain: On a stream, dropDuplicates keeps state across triggers, bounded by withWatermark().

questions.q: A dashboard needs a fast, approximate distinct count of users. Which function fits?

options.why: summary gives count, mean and others, not distinct counts.

questions.explain: approx_count_distinct estimates a distinct count (relative standard deviation 0.05 by default).

questions.q: A running total per customer, ordered by date, is needed on every row. Which frame fits SUM() OVER (PARTITION BY customer ORDER BY d ...)?

options.t: No ORDER BY and no frame
options.why: That sums the whole partition on every row.
That is a three-row moving sum.

options.t: `ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW`
`ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING`
options.why: That sums the rest of the rows.

questions.explain: Aggregate functions can be window functions; a frame from unbounded preceding to the current row gives a running total, as in the window page's examples.

questions.q: Which function returns NULL instead of an error when a VARIANT value can't be cast to the requested type?
questions.explain: variant_get raises INVALID_VARIANT_CAST on a failed cast; try_variant_get returns NULL instead.

questions.q: Invalid rows must be kept for inspection instead of written to silver or dropped silently. What does the pipelines page call this pattern?

options.t: Quarantining invalid rows, built on top of expectations
The default warn action, which writes invalid rows aside
options.why: Warn writes invalid rows to the target.

questions.explain: Expectations warn, drop or fail; quarantining invalid rows is an advanced pattern built on top.

questions.q: Bad updates were applied to some rows. Which fixes them from an earlier version without restoring the whole table?

options.t: `MERGE INTO t USING t TIMESTAMP AS OF <before>` on the affected keys
`DESCRIBE HISTORY t`, then UPDATE each affected row by hand from the old values

questions.explain: The history page lists MERGE ... USING t TIMESTAMP AS OF for bad updates and INSERT ... SELECT ... TIMESTAMP AS OF for deleted rows.

questions.q: A table has deletion vectors. A DELETE removes a customer's rows. What does the data file holding them look like afterwards?

options.t: Deleted, with the other rows copied to a new file
options.why: That is what deletion vectors avoid.

options.t: Rewritten at once without the deleted rows, then committed
options.why: With deletion vectors the file isn't rewritten.

options.t: Unchanged, with the rows marked deleted in metadata

options.why: That is change data feed's folder.

questions.explain: Deletion vectors mark rows in metadata and readers apply the mark at query time; OPTIMIZE, REORG ... APPLY (PURGE) or auto compaction apply them physically.

questions.q: A column holds an array of items. Which function returns one row per element?

options.why: It does not return a row per element; explode does.
split makes an array from a string.

questions.explain: explode(col) returns one row per array element (or map entry).

questions.q: Which call keeps only rows with at least two non-null values?

options.why: That drops only rows where every value is null.
That drops a row with any null.

questions.explain: dropna(thresh=n) keeps rows with at least n non-null values and overrides how.
